trigger: srcWithMext Verilator PASS but board still reports wrong SEG/fail symbol; routed timing report shows CDC timing violation

files_modified.notes: Restored DRAM read response and byte-offset alignment to one cycle after checking the generated Vivado wrapper reports READ_LATENCY=1.

Set DRAM_0 Register_PortA_Output_of_Memory_Primitives=false and generate a late CDC XDC that groups clk_out1_pll and clk_out2_pll asynchronously; removed Tcl if/else from the generated XDC because Vivado ignored those commands during implementation.
Updated the already-generated build constraint file to the same plain XDC set_clock_groups command so the current project can be reimplemented without regenerating from Tcl first.
Split counter reset into cpu_rst and cnt_rst so each clock domain uses a reset synchronized to that domain; marked CDC synchronizer stages with ASYNC_REG.
Added a 50 MHz synchronized mirror for slow status signals feeding twin_controller; later static review found the dynamically scanned SEG bus must not be crossed this way.
Marked reset, virtual switch, and key synchronizer stages with ASYNC_REG.

Connected counter CPU-side reset to the CPU domain reset and counter-side reset to the 50 MHz counter domain reset; moved SEG scan generation to the 50 MHz domain after synchronizing the raw seg_wdata register, avoiding bitwise CDC of the dynamic 40-bit scanned SEG bus.
Updated the legacy counter instantiation to the split-reset interface to avoid future recursive-compile port mismatches.

Corrected the DRAM timing contract to one-cycle READ_LATENCY, documented generated C_READ_LATENCY_A as the source of truth, and recorded the routed timing evidence for the clk_out2_pll -> clk_out1_pll CDC failure.
Recorded the second board-debug pass and backup location.

verification: Static review: generated fpga/build/.../DRAM_0.v reports X_INTERFACE READ_LATENCY 1 and C_READ_LATENCY_A=1.
Static review: generated IROM_0 also reports READ_LATENCY 1, matching the current fetch-side assumption.

Static review: existing fpga/build/digital_twin_srcWithMext/pll.xci still shows CLKOUT2_REQUESTED_OUT_FREQ=80.000, so that build is stale or was generated with FPGA_CPU_CLK_MHZ=80 rather than the current Tcl default of 50.
Static review: existing routed timing report says Timing constraints are not met; clk_out2_pll -> clk_out1_pll has WNS=-0.131ns/TNS=-0.750ns across 9 failing endpoints.

Routed timing report fpga/build/digital_twin_srcWithMext/digital_twin.runs/impl_1/top_timing_summary_routed.rpt shows intra-clock timing is met: clk_out2_pll WNS=+0.433ns and clk_out1_pll WNS=+16.730ns. The only failing setup path is inter-clock clk_out2_pll -> clk_out1_pll with WNS=-0.029ns.

The failing endpoint in that report is student_top_inst/mem_bridge/seg_driver/count_reg[4] to virtual_seg_50_d1_reg[12], confirming the old build was timing the dynamically scanned SEG bus across CPU and 50 MHz domains.

Implementation runme.log reports CRITICAL WARNING [Designutils 20-1307]: Command 'if' is not supported in the XDC constraint file digital_twin_cdc.xdc, so the previous asynchronous clock grouping did not take effect.

Static review after srcWithMext Verilator PASS: top-level still crossed the continuously changing 40-bit scanned SEG bus from CPU clock to 50 MHz for twin_controller. This can produce incoherent segment snapshots on FPGA even when the CPU program passes.
notes: Current evidence points to board-only CDC/IP-alignment risks, not a CPU core frequency bottleneck. The routed design failed because a stale/old SEG scan path crossed from clk_out2_pll to clk_out1_pll and because the generated CDC XDC used unsupported Tcl control flow, preventing set_clock_groups from applying. Rebuild from clean RTL/Tcl after these fixes and re-check runme.log for zero XDC critical warnings plus timing summary with no inter-clock setup violations.
